Title: [PDF] Speculative Speculative Decoding - arXiv
URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03251
Content: 6 4.1 Predicting Verification Outcomes: Building the Saguaro Cache Given a speculation sT that is in the process of being verified, Saguaro must build a cache ST for the most likely verification outcomes. The difficulty is that the space of possible verification outcomes is vast, of size approximately (K + 1)V where V is the model vocabulary size. Since there are O(KV ) potential verification outcomes, it is impractical to preemptively speculate for all of them in parallel. This motivates posing verification prediction as constrained optimization: given a budget of B verification outcomes, how should one select them to maximize the chances of a cache hit? Note that the budget B typically corresponding to the maximum number of outcomes the draft can finish speculating for before [...] 4.2.2 Theoretical Results Theorem 15. For fan-out F and primary speculator logits z, the cache hit rate phit of the Saguaro sampling scheme increases monotonically as C →0.
The new sampling hyperparameter C allows a trade-off between cache hit rate and acceptance rate.
We plot this tradeoff in Figure 5 (left).
Figure 5 (right) presents an illustration of how Saguaro sampling allows control of the residual distribution by manipulating the draft distribution during speculation. [...] Cache Figure 5: We introduce Saguaro sampling, a novel sampling scheme designed specifically for SSD.

Title: [PDF] Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Reinforcement Learning - arXiv

Content: 7 CONCLUSION In this paper, we introduce LTD, a novel speculative decoding method that directly optimizes the throughput of each draft-and-verify cycle using reinforcement learning. By employing two co-adaptive policies to dynamically coordinate the drafting and verification phases, LTD learns to manage the trade-off between acceptance length and time cost, achieving a synergistic acceleration. Extensive experiments on five distinct LLMs across four benchmarks demonstrate that LTD consistently achieves state-of-the-art acceleration for both greedy decoding and high-temperature sampling. This superior performance underscores the effectiveness and robustness of our approach, positioning LTD as a powerful solution for accelerating LLM inference. [...] Based the idea above, we propose LTD (learning to draft), a novel method that synergistically optimizes both phases by using throughput as the direct optimization objective. Specifically, we formulate the interaction between the draft and target models as a reinforcement learning (RL) environment. As shown in Figure 1, we train two distinct, co-adaptive policies: a depth policy to control draft cost by determining the draft tree’s depth, and a size policy that manages verification cost by selecting the optimal number of candidate tokens for the target model. Crucially, these policies are trained using the throughput of each draft-and-verify cycle as a direct reward signal. Title: ICLR Poster Speculative Speculative Decoding - ICLR 2026
URL: https://iclr.cc/virtual/2026/poster/10008711
Content: Autoregressive decoding is bottlenecked by its sequential nature. Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate inference by using a fast draft model to predict upcoming tokens from a slower target model, and then verifying them in parallel with a single target model forward pass. However, speculative decoding itself relies on a sequential dependence between speculation and verification. We introduce speculative speculative decoding (SSD) to parallelize these operations. While a verification is ongoing, the draft model predicts likely verification outcomes and prepares speculations pre-emptively for them. If the actual verification outcome is then in the predicted set, a speculation can be returned immediately, eliminating drafting overhead entirely. We identify three key [...] drafting overhead entirely. We identify three key challenges presented by speculative speculative decoding, and suggest principled methods to solve each. The result is Saguaro, an optimized SSD algorithm. Our implementation is up to 2x faster than optimized speculative decoding baselines and up to 5x faster than autoregressive decoding with open source inference engines.

Title: ICLR Oral Overcoming Joint Intractability with Lossless Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
URL: https://iclr.cc/virtual/2026/oral/10010024
Content: Verification is a key bottleneck in improving inference speed while maintaining distribution fidelity in Speculative Decoding. Recent work has shown that sequence-level verification leads to a higher number of accepted tokens compared to token-wise verification. However, existing solutions often rely on surrogate approximations or are constrained by partial information, struggling with joint intractability. In this work, we propose \emph{Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (HSD)}, a provably lossless verification method that significantly boosts the expected number of accepted tokens and overcomes joint intractability by balancing excess and deficient probability mass across accessible branches. Our extensive large-scale experiments demonstrate that HSD yields consistent improvements in [...] demonstrate that HSD yields consistent improvements in acceptance rates across diverse model families and benchmarks. Moreover, its strong explainability and generality make it readily integrable into a wide range of speculative decoding frameworks. Notably, integrating HSD into EAGLE-3 yields over a 12\% performance gain, establishing state-of-the-art decoding efficiency without compromising distribution fidelity. Title: [PDF] Overcoming Joint Intractability with Lossless Hierarchical ... - arXiv
URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.05724
Content: On average, HSD provides consistent advantages over Tokenwise and Blockwise verification, with improvements of approximately 6.2% in BE and 6.7% in DS. [...] In summary, our contributions are as follows: • We introduce Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (HSD), a lossless and explainable verifica-tion method that integrates seamlessly with existing speculative decoding frameworks while remaining largely orthogonal to them.
• HSD delivers a practical advance in inference scaling, achieving an average 6.7% im-provement in decoding speed across diverse benchmarks and model sizes while preserving distributional fidelity, with efficiency gains of up to 12.3% on individual datasets.
• HSD further improves decoding speed across multi-draft settings. Notably, integrating HSD into EAGLE-3 yields over 12% performance gain, establishing new state-of-the-art decoding efficiency without compromising distribution fidelity. [...] 4 THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS OF HIERARCHICAL SPECULATIVE DECODING For any lossless speculative decoding, the probability of generating an output decomposes into two parts: (1) the probability a draft is accepted, becoming the final output, and (2) the probability a draft is rejected, triggering a corrective resampling step. In token-wise speculative decoding, resampling is straightforward because each token’s probability is directly accessible. In contrast, full joint probabilities over sequences are intractable for auto-regressive models. Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (HSD) overcomes this via hierarchical branch resampling, where multiple resampling distributions at different levels recover partial target distributions, which together statistically recover the full distribution. This

Title: Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (HSD) - Emergent Mind
URL: https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/hierarchical-speculative-decoding-hsd
Content: The theoretical correctness of HSD is supported via proofs of losslessness: so long as verification steps at each level are properly orchestrated (including bottom-up sequence-level checks and probabilistic acceptance as in Traversal Verification (Weng et al., 18 May 2025)), the output distribution exactly matches that of the full target model. HSD is not strictly limited to Transformers; extensions to state-space models and hybrid architectures (e.g., via STree (Wu et al., 20 May 2025) and Mamba Drafters (Choi et al., 1 Jun 2025)) enable efficient speculative tree decoding with constant or sub-linear memory scaling. [...] A common recursive template for HSD (as formalized in (Globerson et al., 22 Oct 2025)) is as follows: Let a hierarchy of models {M₀ (fastest), ..., M\_K (target)} be given.

 M₀ generates T₀ tokens autoregressively.
 For each 1 ≤ i ≤ K, model Mᵢ verifies the buffer from M\_{i−1} (using e.g., a rejection sampling rule or divergence threshold), buffering Tᵢ accepted tokens, requesting more as needed.
 M\_K performs final verification, ensuring output correctness.

The expected latency per generated token can be expressed as:

L=i=0∑K​ci​j=i∏K​R(αj−1,j​,j) [...] Asynchronous and Parallel Token Processing: Architectures such as SwiftSpec (Zhang et al., 12 Jun 2025) and PipeSpec (McDanel et al., 2 May 2025) split draft and target processes across disaggregated hardware, overlapping computation and communication using parallel tree generation, tree-aware KV cache layout, and custom kernel fusion to minimize latency per token and maximize hardware utilization.
 Verification Algorithms: Traversal Verification (Weng et al., 18 May 2025) generalizes token-wise checking to sequence-level (bottom-up) verification, supporting tree-structured speculative drafts and improving acceptance lengths and throughput, especially in high-diversity generation settings.

Verification has traditionally relied on strict, lossless checks (Stern et al., 2018; Xia et al., 2023), ensuring equivalence to q but incurring rollback overhead. Lossy veri-fication (Leviathan et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2023) relaxes acceptance rules, tolerating bounded divergence across tiers to improve efficiency. Cascades (Chen et al., 2025b; Narasimhan et al., 2025) reframes cascading as target-distribution selection, embedding deferral policies within SD. Token tree verification (Miao et al., 2023; Cai et al., 2024; Li et al., 2024) further parallelizes the process by validating multiple candidate paths.

Compared to decoding without drafting, HVSD provides 2.5-3× acceleration while improving output quality. Our results establish multi-tier SD as a general paradigm for scalable and efficient LLM inference. [...] Abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) addresses the high inference costs of large language models by having lightweight drafters generate candidates for large verifiers to validate in parallel. Current draft-verify methods use binary decisions: accept or fully recompute. We find that current binary verification creates inefficiency: many rejected tokens could be verified correctly with a slim model rather than a full verifier. This motivates our Training-Free Slim-Verifier to handle tokens requiring moderate verification resources, reducing expensive large-model calls. We propose Hierarchical Verification for Speculative Decoding (HVSD), a three-tier training-free framework using a skip-layer slim-verifier. [...] Current Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification methods predict reasoning correctness based on outputs (black-box) or activations (gray-box), but offer limited insight into \textit{why} a computation fails. We introduce a white-box method: \textbf{Circuit-based Reasoning Verification (CRV)}. We hypothesize that attribution graphs of correct CoT steps, viewed as \textit{execution traces} of the model's latent reasoning circuits, possess distinct structural fingerprints from those of incorrect steps. By training a classifier on structural features of these graphs, we show that these traces contain a powerful signal of reasoning errors. Our white-box approach yields novel scientific insights unattainable by other methods. (1) We demonstrate that structural signatures of error are highly [...] to extrapolate from an 8K context to a 3.5M QA task with a performance loss of less than 10\% and achieving over 95\% on the 512K NIAH test.

### Carlos

AI Agent at UBOS [...] Speculative Decoding illustration

## 1. Introduction

The AI research community has long grappled with the latency bottleneck inherent in autoregressive decoding of transformer models. As large language models (LLMs) grow in size, the sequential nature of token‑by‑token generation becomes a critical obstacle for real‑time applications such as chat assistants, code completion, and interactive storytelling. The newly released arXiv paper Speculative Decoding (arXiv:2603.03251) proposes a bold extension—Speculative Speculative Decoding (SSD)—that pushes the parallelism frontier even further. In this article we unpack the core ideas, highlight the main contributions, and explore why SSD matters for fast text generation, AI research, and production‑grade NLP pipelines. [...] | Model | Baseline (AR) Latency | Speculative Decoding | SSD (Saguaro) | Perplexity Δ |
 ---  --- 
| GPT‑2‑XL | 120 ms | 68 ms (1.76×) | 45 ms (2.67×) | +0.3 |
| LLaMA‑7B | 210 ms | 115 ms (1.82×) | 78 ms (2.69×) | +0.2 |
| Proprietary 30B | 560 ms | 310 ms (1.81×) | 210 ms (2.67×) | +0.1 |

Across all three model families, SSD consistently outperforms both the vanilla autoregressive baseline and the earlier speculative decoding approach. Notably, the perplexity increase is negligible (< 0.3), confirming that speed gains do not come at the cost of generation fidelity.

UBOS engineers have already integrated a Workflow automation studio that can orchestrate the three parallel streams required by SSD, allowing data scientists to spin up a “speculative inference” pipeline with a few clicks.

Title: Speculative Decoding Optimizations by Tri Dao et al | Jawad Md posted on the topic | LinkedIn
URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mdjawad_inference-llm-activity-7435917782883528705-rpQZ
Content: I published a deep dive on Speculative Speculative Decoding, the ICLR 2026 paper by Tri Dao, Tanishq Kumar, Avner May that finds and eliminates a hidden bottleneck inside speculative decoding itself.
Core insight: while the target model verifies draft tokens, the draft model sits completely idle. SSD puts that wasted time to work by predicting verification outcomes and pre-computing the next speculation in advance. When the prediction is right, the next round starts instantly. [...] When the average attention score across tokens is low, the softmax still needs to sum to 1. In these uncertain situations, models seem to exhibit a bias toward the initial tokens in the sequence (often instruction tokens or special markers). So when the model isn’t strongly confident about where to attend, those early tokens tend to absorb more attention.
The idea is simple: introduce a few special tokens at the beginning of the sequence that are always kept in the KV cache.
These tokens act as attention sinks. Because they consistently attract attention, they help stabilize the softmax denominator, making the attention distribution more stable even when the context window slides.
Simple idea, but an elegant explanation of a behavior many of us have observed in long-context inference. [...] This builds directly on our earlier post covering standard speculative decoding. I spent some time on interactive visualizations for this one. There's a fan-out grid that shows exactly what "caching bonus token predictions" means before any math appears, distribution plots where you can drag a slider and watch the residual concentrate onto cached tokens, and a fallback chart that makes the exponential batch-size problem visceral. The goal was to make every concept in the paper something you can see and play with, not just read about.
If you found the original speculative decoding post useful, this is the natural next step.

## Speculative Speculative Decoding

### Tanishq Kumar, Tri Dao, Avner May

Published: 26 Jan 2026, Last Modified: 02 Mar 2026ICLR 2026 PosterEveryoneRevisionsBibTeXCC BY 4.0

Keywords: inference, large language models, speculative decoding

TL;DR: We introduce an asynchronous speculative decoding algorithm wherein the draft model continuously speculates on top of anticipated verification outcomes, thus hiding drafting latency entirely. [...] Abstract: Autoregressive decoding is bottlenecked by its \sequential\ nature. Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate inference by using a fast draft model to predict upcoming tokens from a slower target model, and then verifying them \in parallel\ with a single target model forward pass. However, speculative decoding itself relies on a \sequential\ dependence between speculation and verification. We introduce \speculative speculative decoding\ (SSD) to parallelize these operations. While a verification is ongoing, the draft model \predicts\ likely verification outcomes and prepares speculations pre-emptively for them. If the actual verification outcome is then in the predicted set, a speculation can be returned immediately, eliminating drafting overhead entirely. We [...] immediately, eliminating drafting overhead entirely. We identify three key challenges presented by speculative speculative decoding, and suggest principled methods to solve each. The result is Saguaro, an optimized SSD algorithm. Our implementation is up to 2x faster than optimized speculative decoding baselines and up to 5x faster than autoregressive decoding with open source inference engines.

# Speculative Speculative Decoding

### Paper



"In all fictions, each time a man meets diverse alternatives, he chooses one and eliminates the others; in the work of the almost unfathomable Ts'ui Pên, he chooses — simultaneously — all of them."

— Jorge Luis Borges, "The Garden of Forking Paths" (1941)

SSD is a new LLM inference algorithm. It is exact, and it is extremely fast.

SSD is a new type of speculative decoding (SD). In normal SD, a small and fast model guesses the next few tokens that a larger slower model may generate, and the large model then verifies them in one forward pass: drafting and verification happen one after the other on the same hardware. ## Usage

All commands below run from inside the `bench/` directory. Large models (Llama-3 70B, Qwen-3 32B) take a few minutes for load/warmup/compile before generation starts. Always use `python -O` to disable debug overhead.

### Benchmarks

Use `--all` for full eval across four datasets. Since different data distributions are predictable to varying degrees, the speed of SD/SSD depends a lot on the dataset. Averaging over many prompts from many types of datasets
gives an overall picture. `--numseqs` is per-dataset, so `--numseqs 128 --all` runs 128 × 4 = 512 prompts total.

## 1. Core Performance Results

SSD achieves up to 2× speedup over optimized speculative decoding (SD) and up to 5× over autoregressive (AR) decoding (Figure 7, Table B.3).

Title: Speculative Speculative Decoding | Papers | HyperAI
URL: https://hyper.ai/en/papers/2603.03251
Content: The authors leverage speculative speculative decoding (SSD) to break the sequential dependency between drafting and verification inherent in traditional speculative decoding. In SSD, while the target model is verifying a current speculation, the draft model runs asynchronously on a separate device to predict likely verification outcomes—defined by the number of accepted tokens and the sampled bonus token—and pre-speculates token sequences for each of these outcomes in parallel. If the actual verification outcome matches one of the precomputed outcomes, the corresponding speculation is returned immediately, eliminating the need for on-the-fly drafting and reducing latency. This framework is lossless and requires the draft model to reside on distinct hardware from the target, enabling true [...] The authors leverage speculative speculative decoding (SSD) to break the sequential dependency between drafting and verification inherent in traditional speculative decoding. In SSD, while the target model is verifying a current speculation, the draft model runs asynchronously on a separate device to predict likely verification outcomes—defined by the number of accepted tokens and the sampled bonus token—and pre-speculates token sequences for each of these outcomes in parallel. If the actual verification outcome matches one of the precomputed outcomes, the corresponding speculation is returned immediately, eliminating the need for on-the-fly drafting and reducing latency. This framework is lossless and requires the draft model to reside on distinct hardware from the target, enabling true [...] To implement this, the authors introduce SAGUARO, an optimized SSD algorithm that addresses three core challenges: predicting verification outcomes accurately, balancing cache hit rate against speculation quality, and handling cache misses efficiently. The speculation cache, a key component, maps each possible verification outcome vT=(k,t∗) to a precomputed speculation sT. During verification of round T, the draft model predicts a set of likely outcomes VT and speculates for each in parallel, storing results in the cache. Upon receiving the actual outcome, the system performs a cache lookup: if the outcome is present, the precomputed tokens are returned; otherwise, a fallback strategy is invoked.

## Metadata [...] ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

# Motivation

vLLM already supports speculative decoding to accelerate autoregressive generation using a draft model. However, speculative decoding still suffers from a sequential dependency between drafting and verification: the draft model must wait for the target model to finish verifying tokens before generating the next speculation batch.

Recent work proposes Speculative Speculative Decoding (SSD), which removes this dependency by running drafting and verification asynchronously and precomputing speculations for predicted verification outcomes.

Content: + Crucially, LTD maintains its effectiveness and delivers an approximate 5% throughput gain even in high-temperature sampling scenarios (Temperature=1.0), where many other dynamic speculative decoding methods experience significant performance degradation. This robustness highlights LTD's ability to generalize beyond greedy decoding and adapt to more stochastic generation environments, a key challenge for existing dynamic approaches. [...] Figure 1: The overview of LTD method. We formulate the interaction between draft model and target model as an RL environment. We employ two policies to dynamically manage the allocation between draft generation and target verification by controlling the draft tree’s depth and verification size. These policies are optimized together using the reward signal based on the throughput of each draft-and-verify cycle.

 We introduce Learning to Draft (LTD), a novel method that formulates speculative decoding as a reinforcement learning environment to directly optimize throughput for each draft-and-verify cycle.

 LTD employs a co-adaptive policy framework, training a depth policy and a size policy to dynamically manage draft tree depth and verification size, respectively. Title: [PDF] Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Reinforcement Learning - arXiv
URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01639
Content: 7 CONCLUSION In this paper, we introduce LTD, a novel speculative decoding method that directly optimizes the throughput of each draft-and-verify cycle using reinforcement learning. By employing two co-adaptive policies to dynamically coordinate the drafting and verification phases, LTD learns to manage the trade-off between acceptance length and time cost, achieving a synergistic acceleration. Extensive experiments on five distinct LLMs across four benchmarks demonstrate that LTD consistently achieves state-of-the-art acceleration for both greedy decoding and high-temperature sampling. This superior performance underscores the effectiveness and robustness of our approach, positioning LTD as a powerful solution for accelerating LLM inference. [...] Based the idea above, we propose LTD (learning to draft), a novel method that synergistically optimizes both phases by using throughput as the direct optimization objective. Specifically, we formulate the interaction between the draft and target models as a reinforcement learning (RL) environment. As shown in Figure 1, we train two distinct, co-adaptive policies: a depth policy to control draft cost by determining the draft tree’s depth, and a size policy that manages verification cost by selecting the optimal number of candidate tokens for the target model. Crucially, these policies are trained using the throughput of each draft-and-verify cycle as a direct reward signal. Furthermore, we train these two policies iteratively, which allows them to co-adapt to each other’s evolving [...] 3.52 5.29 4.05 5.97 Iter3 4.05 6.32 4.98 8.53 3.98 6.00 3.62 5.37 4.16 6.08 A.6 INTERACTION BETWEEN THE DEPTH AND SIZE POLICIES To validate the effectiveness of our iterative training, we analyzed the test set distributions of the initial separately trained policies (’Iter0’) and the final iteratively trained LTD policies, as shown in Figure 6. Specifically, we examined the relationship between the number of candidate tokens and the draft depth conditioned on the acceptance length. As observed, Iter0 exhibits a static pattern regardless of acceptance length, predominantly clustering in the region where the draft depth is < 6 and the token count is < 60. Instances with a shallow depth (< 6) but a large token budget (> 60) are negligible. In contrast, LTD demonstrates superior adaptability

Title: 1 Introduction - arXiv

Content: Motivated by the above-mentioned gaps and opportunities, we introduce ReSpec, a system that adapts speculative decoding to the unique demands of RL training. ReSpec provides three targeted mechanisms, each directly addressing one of the gaps (Figure 1 (b)). Specifically, (1) for G1, we design Adaptive Speculative Decoding Server. It dynamically selects and applies speculative-decoding configurations based on lightweight profiling and runtime workload signals. (2) For G2, we introduce Drafter Evolution via Knowledge Distillation with a Online Learner. To keep the drafter aligned with the continually updated actor, we evolve the drafter using on-policy distillation from the actor. This distillation pipeline continuously transfers the actor’s distributional knowledge into the lightweight [...] ## 7 Conclusion

We present ReSpec, the first system that adapts speculative decoding to reinforcement learning for large language models. By addressing key bottlenecks—diminishing speedups, drafter staleness, and policy degradation—ReSpec integrates adaptive decoding, drafter evolution, and reward-weighted adaptation. Experiments on Qwen models show up to 4.5×4.5\times faster training with stable reward convergence, demonstrating the practicality of ReSpec for scalable and efficient RL training.

## References

Mascot Sammy [...] Figure 3 illustrates a concrete instance: a drafter may repeatedly propose a superficially plausible phrase that yields lower downstream reward than the actor’s optimal continuation (e.g., “the key to success” vs. “the key of life”), and these accepted drafts accumulate in the replay buffer. Empirically, we observe that naively applying EAGLE-3 in our RL runs can produce a measurable drop in reward after on the order of 100 update steps (Figure 5), consistent with drafter-induced distributional bias harming learning.

## Speculative Speculative Decoding

Download PDF

### Tanishq Kumar, Tri Dao, Avner May

Published: 26 Jan 2026, Last Modified: 02 Mar 2026ICLR 2026 PosterEveryoneRevisionsBibTeXCC BY 4.0

Keywords: inference, large language models, speculative decoding

TL;DR: We introduce an asynchronous speculative decoding algorithm wherein the draft model continuously speculates on top of anticipated verification outcomes, thus hiding drafting latency entirely. [...] immediately, eliminating drafting overhead entirely. We identify three key challenges presented by speculative speculative decoding, and suggest principled methods to solve each. The result is Saguaro, an optimized SSD algorithm. Our implementation is up to 2x faster than optimized speculative decoding baselines and up to 5x faster than autoregressive decoding with open source inference engines. [...] Abstract: Autoregressive decoding is bottlenecked by its \sequential\ nature. Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate inference by using a fast draft model to predict upcoming tokens from a slower target model, and then verifying them \in parallel\ with a single target model forward pass. However, speculative decoding itself relies on a \sequential\ dependence between speculation and verification. We introduce \speculative speculative decoding\ (SSD) to parallelize these operations. While a verification is ongoing, the draft model \predicts\ likely verification outcomes and prepares speculations pre-emptively for them. If the actual verification outcome is then in the predicted set, a speculation can be returned immediately, eliminating drafting overhead entirely. We

Title: ICML Poster BanditSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via Bandit Algorithms
URL: https://icml.cc/virtual/2025/poster/44460
Content: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, generate text by predicting one word at a time, which can be slow. A method called speculative decoding speeds this up by using a lightweight “draft” model to guess several words ahead, then verifying them with the full model. However, current speculative decoding methods often use a fixed setup for all prompts, regardless of the task — whether it’s writing code or generating stories. This limits their effectiveness. Our work introduces BanditSpec, a smarter and more adaptive speculative decoding framework inspired by multi-armed bandit algorithms — a type of decision-making strategy that balances exploration and exploitation. BanditSpec dynamically learns which decoding configuration works best for each prompt as generation progresses, [...] Speculative decoding has emerged as a popular method to accelerate the inference of Large Language Models (LLMs) while retaining their superior text generation performance. Previous methods either adopt a fixed speculative decoding configuration regardless of the prefix tokens, or train draft models in an offline or online manner to align them with the context. This paper proposes a training-free online learning framework to adaptively choose the configuration of the hyperparameters for speculative decoding as text is being generated. We first formulate this hyperparameter selection problem as a Multi-Armed Bandit problem and provide a general speculative decoding framework BanditSpec. Furthermore, two bandit-based hyperparameter selection algorithms, UCBSpec and EXP3Spec, are designed [...] works best for each prompt as generation progresses, without requiring extra training. We design two algorithms, UCBSpec and EXP3Spec, that select the best setup in real time. Experiments with popular models like LLaMA3 and Qwen2 show that BanditSpec significantly improves text generation speed and closely matches the performance of the best possible fixed setup (the "oracle"). In summary, BanditSpec makes LLMs faster by learning how to guess better -- on the fly.

In summary, our contributions are as follows: • We introduce Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (HSD), a lossless and explainable verifica-tion method that integrates seamlessly with existing speculative decoding frameworks while remaining largely orthogonal to them.
• HSD delivers a practical advance in inference scaling, achieving an average 6.7% im-provement in decoding speed across diverse benchmarks and model sizes while preserving distributional fidelity, with efficiency gains of up to 12.3% on individual datasets.
• HSD further improves decoding speed across multi-draft settings. Notably, integrating HSD into EAGLE-3 yields over 12% performance gain, establishing new state-of-the-art decoding efficiency without compromising distribution fidelity.

###### Definition 5.

A cache hit is when the outcome \mathit{v}^{T} of verifying \mathit{s}^{T-1} is contained in the speculation cache \mathcal{S}^{T}. A cache miss is when \mathit{v}^{T}\notin\mathcal{S}^{T}.

###### Definition 6.

Let \mathbf{p_{\mathrm{hit,p}}} denote the probability of a cache hit on an iteration conditional on the previous iteration having been speculated by the primary speculator. Analogously, \mathbf{p_{\mathrm{hit,b}}} represents the probability of a cache hit on an iteration conditional on speculating with the backup model. 现在我有了三篇论文的充分细节，下面给出详细讲解。

---

## HSD — Hierarchical Speculative Decoding（ICLR 2026 Oral）

**论文**：arXiv:2601.05724，周宇轩等，阿里 Qwen 团队

### 核心问题

传统 SD 的 verify 分 token-wise 和 block-wise 两种。token-wise 对每个 token 独立接受/拒绝，不利用序列级联合概率；block-wise 试图做序列级验证，但面临 **联合不可行性**（joint intractability）——自回归模型的联合概率 `p(X₁:t)` 在树形 draft 结构上无法精确计算，所以现有方法要么用代理近似，要么只用部分信息。

### 核心思想：层次分支重采样

HSD 的关键洞察：**验证被拒绝时，重采样分布不需要恢复完整的 target 分布，只需要恢复本分支内的"亏损"部分**。

具体来说，当 draft 序列 `X₁:γ` 从后往前扫描被拒绝在位置 τ 时：

1. **接受阶段**：从 γ→1 反向扫描，对每个位置 t 计算 `h_t = p(x_t|X₁:t₋₁) / q(x_t|X₁:t₋₁)`。若 `h_t ≥ η_t`（均匀采样），接受；否则拒绝并记录 τ。
2. **重采样阶段**：在位置 τ+1，不需要从完整 target 分布采样，而是用**层次化的分支重采样分布** `P*_res(·|X₁:τ)`，只恢复 target 在当前分支上超出 draft 的那部分概率质量（excess probability mass），同时把被丢弃路径的概率质量（deficient probability mass）重分配回来。

### 为什么无损？

论文证明：HSD 的输出分布精确等于 target 分布。关键推导：

```
P(x_t is yielded) = q(x_t)·h(x_t) + D_KL(q,p)·p(x_t) - q(x_t)·h(x_t)/D_KL(p,q) = p(x_t)
```

即接受路径和重采样路径的概率加权和恰好等于 target 概率。层次分支结构保证了每个分支的重采样分布只恢复局部亏损，但所有分支的期望加起来恢复全局分布。

### Capped Branch Resampling

朴素 HSD 在被拒绝后需要对 τ+1 到 γ 的每个位置都调用 target model 重采样（γ-τ+1 次调用），代价高昂。Capped Branch Resampling 的关键改进：**只在 τ+1 位置做一次重采样**，后续位置用 draft 分布的条件继续。这在不损失正确性的前提下把额外调用降到 O(1)。

### 与 EAGLE-3 集成

HSD 替换 EAGLE-3 的 tokenwise verifier。注意 EAGLE-3 用 top-K 采样做 draft（所有 draft 概率等于 1），理论上任何验证方法在这种设置下退化为相同行为。但 HSD 的**实现避免了 EAGLE 原始 tokenwise 验证中的显式循环**，所以即使理论上等价，实际速度仍有 12%+ 提升。

### 实验结果

| 指标 | 改善幅度 |
|---|---|
| Block Efficiency (BE) | 平均 +6.2% vs tokenwise |
| Decoding Speed (DS) | 平均 +6.7% vs tokenwise |
| HumanEval 32B DS | +11.4% |
| EAGLE-3 集成 | **+12%** |
| Multi-draft (11 candidates) | BE +5.9%, DS +4.7% |

实验用 Qwen2.5 (0.5B draft / 14B-72B target)，单 H20 GPU。

## SSD/Saguaro — Speculative Speculative Decoding（ICLR 2026 Poster）

**论文**：arXiv:2603.03251，Tanishq Kumar, Tri Dao, Avner May

### 核心问题

标准 SD 中 draft 和 verify 是**串行**的：draft model 生成 → target model verify → draft model 再生成 → …。verify 期间 draft model 完全空闲。

### 核心思想：对 verify 结果做推测

SSD 让 draft model 在 target verify 的**同时**，预测 verify 可能的结果，并**提前为每种结果准备好下一轮 speculation**。如果实际 verify 结果命中了预测集，直接返回预计算的 draft token，消除了 draft 延迟。

verification outcome 定义为 `(k, t*)`：k = 被接受的 token 数，t* = bonus token。例如 γ=5 时，可能的结果有 (0,t₁), (1,t₂), ..., (5,t₆) 等。

### Saguaro 三个关键组件

**1. Saguaro Cache（几何扇出缓存）**

不是均匀地为每种 verify 结果分配预计算预算，而是用**几何级数**分配：

```
F_k = F_0 · (a_p)^{k/(1+r)}   ∀k < K
F_K = F_0 · (a_p)^{K/(1+r)} · (1-a_p)^{-1/(1+r)}
```

其中 `a_p` 是接受率，`r` 是 cache hit rate 的幂律指数。直觉：靠近根的分支（高接受率结果）获得更多预算，因为更可能命中。论文证明这是约束 `ΣF_k ≤ B` 下的最优分配（Theorem 12）。

**2. Saguaro Sampling（缓存命中 vs 接受率平衡）**

核心矛盾：draft model 如果偏向选择"已在缓存中"的 token（提高缓存命中率），会降低 accept rate；如果正常采样（高 accept rate），缓存命中率下降。

Saguaro Sampling 引入超参数 `C ∈ [0,1]`，在采样时降低已缓存 token 的概率权重：

```
p'(x) ∝ p(x) · (1 - C · 1_{x ∈ cache})
```

C=0 是标准采样（高 accept rate），C→1 是强缓存偏向。理论分析给出最优 C 值。

**3. Saguaro Fallback（缓存未命中处理）**

当 verify 结果不在缓存中时，fallback 策略取决于 batch size：
- 小 batch：立即用 draft model 重新生成（延迟可接受）
- 大 batch：用 backup model（更小更快的模型）生成一个保守的 speculation，减少等待

### 无损性证明

论文证明 SSD 是精确无损的：即使 draft model 预测的 verify 结果有误，最终输出分布仍与 target model 完全一致。核心论据：预计算的 speculation 只是提前做了本会在下一轮做的计算，如果结果不匹配则丢弃重新来过。

### 硬件需求

SSD **需要 draft model 在独立 GPU 上运行**（与 target model 分离），这样才能真正并行。论文实验用 1×H100 跑 draft + 4×H100 跑 target。

### 实验结果

| Model | AR (tok/s) | SD (tok/s) | SSD (tok/s) | SSD vs SD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-70B/1B | 54.7 | 161.8 | 255.8 | **1.58×** |
| Qwen-3-32B/0.6B | 88.8 | 136.8 | 203.8 | **1.49×** |

比 SD 平均快 30%，比 AR 快 5×。已开源推理引擎（https://github.com/tanishqkumar/ssd）。

## LTD — Learning To Draft（ICLR 2026 Poster）

**论文**：arXiv:2603.01639，张杰彬等，微软 + 北大

### 核心问题

EAGLE-3 等方法用**静态**的 draft 树参数（固定 depth、固定 verification size）。但最优参数随上下文变化：确定性高的段落适合深 draft + 大 verify，不确定性高的段落适合浅 draft + 小 verify。现有动态方法优化的是代理指标（accept rate），不是真正的吞吐，且把 draft 和 verify 当独立问题处理。

### 核心思想：RL 直接优化吞吐

LTD 把 draft-verify 过程建模为 RL 环境，训练两个**协同自适应策略**，直接以每个 cycle 的吞吐为奖励信号。

### 两个策略

**1. Depth Policy π_D（控制 draft 代价）**

- 动作空间：二值 `{0, 1}`——每步 forward 后决定是否继续 draft
- 直觉：类似早停机制，当 draft model 不再自信时停止

**2. Size Policy π_V（控制 verify 代价）**

- 动作空间：离散 `[20, 240]`——选择提交给 target model 的候选 token 数
- 直觉：verify 太多 token 浪费计算，太少浪费 draft 产出

### 状态空间

```
s_t = [D, L, P₁, ..., P_{V_all}]
```

D = 当前 draft depth，L = 上下文长度，P_i = 第 i 个 draft token 的概率（confidence 信号）

### 奖励函数

```
R_t = L_A / (T_draft + T_verify)
```

L_A = 被接受的 token 数，T_draft + T_verify = 总 wall-clock 时间。**直接优化吞吐而非代理指标**。

### 训练方法：PPO + 迭代协同

1. **初始训练**：两个策略独立训练，用 HumanEval 数据集。depth policy 训练 100K 步（size policy 固定为启发式），size policy 训练 100K 步（depth policy 固定为启发式）。
2. **迭代协同训练**：交替冻结一个策略，用 PPO 更新另一个策略。三轮迭代后收敛。

关键发现：**用 accept rate 做奖励会失败**——size policy 会提出过多 token 做 verify（accept rate 高但 verify 时间暴涨，吞吐反而下降）。只有吞吐做奖励才能正确平衡。

### 高温鲁棒性

LTD 在 temperature=1.0 仍保持 ~5% 的吞吐提升，而其他动态方法在高温下严重退化（因为高温下 accept rate 普遍降低，静态方法的固定参数更不匹配，而 LTD 能自适应调整）。

### 实验结果

| Target 模型 | vs EAGLE-3 提升 |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-32B | **+36.4%** |
| Deepseek-Distilled-Llama-8B | +9.5% |
| Llama-3-8B | +6.5% |
| Vicuna-1.3-13B | +5% |
| Qwen3-14B | +4% |

绝对加速比 2.24×–4.32×。基于 EAGLE-3 框架实现，代码已开源。

---

### 三篇论文的定位对比

| | HSD | SSD/Saguaro | LTD |
|---|---|---|---|
| **创新维度** | 验证算法 | 系统调度 | 策略优化 |
| **改什么** | 验证规则（token-wise → 层次分支） | draft-verify 串行 → 并行 | 静态参数 → 动态自适应 |
| **需要额外资源** | 否 | 是（独立 GPU 跑 draft） | 训练时需要（RL 训练），推理时否 |
| **与 EAGLE-3 关系** | 替换 verifier | 正交（可叠加） | 替换参数策略 |
| **对 MiniCPM-SALA 适用性** | 纯算法层改动，可落地 | 需要额外 GPU，单卡不适用 | RL 训练成本，但理念（动态参数）可借鉴 |

9	## 1. Tree Verification 创新
10	
11	### 1.1 Traversal Verification（NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2505.12398）
12	
13	验证方向从 top-down 改为 bottom-up（叶到根），采用序列级接受概率而非逐 token 接受概率。
14	
15	核心机制：传统 top-down 中父节点拒绝则所有子节点丢弃；Traversal 中父节点只在所有子节点均被拒绝后才验证。序列级联合概率 `min(r(X1)*r(X3), 1)` 允许跨步概率补偿（vs 传统 `min(r(X1),1)*min(r(X3),1)`）。
16	
17	数值示例：`r(X1)=0.5, r(X3)=4/3` 时，Traversal P(accept)=0.667 vs 传统 0.5。
18	
19	纯算法层改动，与 FlashInfer 兼容。
20	
21	### 1.2 Dynamic Delayed Tree Expansion（arXiv:2602.16994, 2026.02）
22	
23	系统评估了 Traversal Verification vs OT-based（SpecInfer）验证策略。发现 Traversal 全面优于 OT 方法。OT 方法在树根附近获得高多 token 接受率，但收益在树深处更关键。
24	
25	提出 delayed tree expansion：先 draft 一段单路径，延迟 i.i.d. 分支点。还开发动态神经选择器（neural selector），从 draft/target 特征估计 OT 验证的 block efficiency，动态决定是否展开。
26	
27	neural selector 需轻量训练；delayed expansion 本身不需要。
28	
29	### 1.3 GOOSE — Anisotropic Speculation Trees（arXiv:2604.02047, 2026.04）
30	
31	观察到两种 training-free token 来源（n-gram 匹配 vs 统计预测）的接受率差距巨大（中位数 6x，范围 2-18x）。**核心定理**：当存在质量差距时，最优树是各向异性的——高接受率 token 形成深链（spine），低接受率 token 作为宽分支。
32	
33	构建自适应 spine tree：深层链由高接受率的 context-matched token 组成，每个节点挂宽分支作备选。5 个 LLM（7B-33B）上比 balanced-tree baseline 提升 12-33%。
34	
35	Training-free。

40

45	利用输出 entropy 作为自然置信度指标（具有跨解码步骤的强时间相关性）。高置信时构建 deep-narrow 树，低置信时构建 shallow-wide 树。

60	
61	### 2.1 MARS — Margin-Aware Speculative Verification（ICLR 2026, arXiv:2601.15498）
62	
63	当 target 的 top-1 和 top-2 概率接近（low-margin）时，拒绝 runner-up token 的信息增益可忽略但 rollback 成本高。MARS 从 target logits 测量 decision stability，低 margin 区域放宽验证。
64	
65	训练免费，域无关，8B-235B 一致提速。

67	### 2.2 Cactus — Constrained Acceptance Speculative Sampling（arXiv:2604.04987, 2026.04）
68	
69	将 speculative sampling 形式化为约束优化问题：最大化 acceptance rate，约束输出分布与 target 的散度 ≤ epsilon。标准 SpS 是 epsilon=0 的特例。
70	
71	接受规则公式（KKT 条件推导）：接受概率 = `min(1, p_target(x)/p_draft(x) * g(x))`，其中 g(x) 保证 `TV(p_output, p_target) ≤ epsilon`。
72	
73	提供 principled 的 epsilon-放松框架。Training-free。
74

76	
77	验证分布从 p_target 放松为 `p_verify = alpha * p_target + (1-alpha) * p_draft`。alpha 由轻量级神经网络学习（单层 FC + sigmoid）。Static Ensemble 变体固定 alpha，training-free。
78	
79	理论保证：relaxed 分布与 target 的偏差有界（TV distance 上界）。
80	
81	代码：https://github.com/comeusr/diversed
82

84	
85	用 importance-weighted resampling 替代 rejection sampling。维护 N 个 draft particles，每步 importance reweight 后 resample，而非拒绝截断。
86	
87	关键洞察：LLM inference 是 memory-bandwidth-bound，SMC 的额外 compute 几乎免费。保留所有 draft 信息，不截断。per-step approximation error 有界（SMC 理论）。
88	
89	Training-free。

98

107	通过 target model 的自监督训练 judge verifier：衡量 token 替换后的 response 是否保持原意。需训练但无需人工标注。

181	## 5. Batch / Parallel Verify
182	
183	### 5.1 MineDraft — Batch Parallel SD（arXiv:2603.18016, 2026.03）
184	
185	维护两批 request，一批 drafting 同时另一批 verification，重叠 drafting latency 与 verification。throughput 提升 75%，latency 降低 39%。已实现为 vLLM 插件。Training-free。
186	
187	### 5.2 ECHO — Elastic Speculative Decoding（arXiv:2604.09603, 2026.04）
188	
189	将 speculative execution 重定义为 budgeted scheduling problem。Sparse confidence gating 将整个 batch 作为统一 super-tree 管理，弹性分配 depth/width budget。已集成在 SGLang 中。Qwen3-235B 上最高 5.35x speedup。Training-free。
190	
191	### 5.3 Mirror-SD — 异构并行（arXiv:2510.13161, 2025.10）
192	
193	draft 和 target 在异构加速器（GPU + NPU）上并行执行。2.8x-5.8x walltime speedup，比 EAGLE-3 平均快 30%。需异构硬件。
194	
195	### 5.4 SpecFormer — 非自回归并行 draft（arXiv:2511.20340, 2025.11）
196	
197	结合单向 + 双向 attention 的 draft 架构。非自回归并行生成消除对大前缀树的依赖。需训练 SpecFormer draft model。
198	
199	---
200	
201	## 6. Verify Overhead / 量化 Verify
202	
203	### 6.1 Quasar — 量化验证（arXiv:2603.01399, 2026.03）
204	
205	对 verification phase 使用低 bit 量化。核心洞察：结构化剪枝严重损害验证准确性，但量化能高保真保留 logit 分布同时减半内存流量。与现有 drafting 策略正交。Training-free。
206	
207	### 6.2 MoE-Spec — Expert Budgeting（arXiv:2602.16052, 2026.02）
208	
209	对 MoE 模型，大 draft tree 激活大量 unique experts 增加内存压力。每层执行固定 expert capacity limit，只加载贡献最大的 experts。比 EAGLE-3 throughput 高 10-30%。Training-free。
210	
211	### 6.3 Nightjar — 自适应 Spec 开关（arXiv:2512.22420, 2025.12）
212	
213	MAB planner 动态决定是否启用 spec decoding。高负载时关闭 SD 并将 draft model offload 到 CPU，回收 GPU 内存给 KV cache。throughput 提升 27.29%，latency 降低 20.18%。Training-free。
214	
215	### 6.4 Hidden State 复用（arXiv:2602.21224, 2026.02）
216	
217	验证失败的 draft hidden states 复用。在 hidden state 层面做自回归预测，验证失败时从 hidden states 重新采样 token 而非从头 draft。最高 3.3x speedup。需训练特殊 draft model。
218	
219	### 6.5 SpeCache — Speculative KV Caching（arXiv:2503.16163, 2025）
220	
221	预测下个 token 可能访问的 KV pair，speculative fetching。低 bit KV cache copy 在 VRAM 中做重要性度量。
222	
223	### 6.6 VOCABTRIM（arXiv:2506.22694, 2025）
224	
225	Draft 时裁剪 LM head 的词汇表，减少不必要的推理开销。对大词表模型（73448）收益显著。Training-free。
226	
227	---
228	
229	## 7. SSM / Mamba + Speculative Decoding Verify
230	
231	### 7.1 SpecMamba（arXiv:2509.19873, 2025）
232	
233	**最直接相关的 SSM verify 工作**。提出 SSM hidden state backtracking 的三种方案：
234	
235	| 方案 | 策略 | 内存开销 | 计算开销 | 适用场景 |
236	|------|------|----------|----------|----------|
237	| Plan I | 存所有 draft token 的 h_t | O(spec_len * state_dim) | 无额外计算 | Draft model |
238	| Plan II | 缓存轻量激活 (A,B,Delta,X)，需时重算 | O(spec_len * activation_dim) | 重算 h_t 的 SSM 前向 | Target verify |
239	| Hybrid | Draft 用 Plan I，Target 用 Plan II | 最优 tradeoff | 最优 tradeoff | 系统级 co-design |
240	
241	FIFO-based Tree Verification with Tiling：利用 SSM 的 token 间依赖关系，按 BFS 顺序验证 tree。节点所有子节点验证完毕后即可驱逐，内存需求从 O(所有节点) 降至 O(活跃路径)。
242	
243	SSM 层无法像 attention 那样对多条候选路径并行计算，必须串行递推。
244	
245	FPGA 上 2.27x 加速。
246	
247	### 7.2 Mamba Drafters（arXiv:2506.01206, 2025, EMNLP 2025）
248	
249	用 Mamba SSM 作为外部 drafter。常数内存 draft（Mamba 的 recurrent state 大小固定）。130M Mamba drafter 在 Llama-2-70B target 上达 2.55x 加速。
250	
251	注意：这是 SSM 做 drafter（target 仍是 Transformer），与 MiniCPM-SALA 的问题方向相反（我们的 target 有 SSM 层）。
252	
253	### 7.3 Gating is Weighting（arXiv:2504.04308, 2025）
254	
255	证明多层 GLA 可实现 Weighted Preconditioned Gradient Descent (WPGD)。Gating 控制每个 token 对预测的贡献权重。
256	
257	对 verify 的含义：GLA state 回滚不只影响"记忆"，还影响模型内部的"优化状态"。如果 state 不完全正确，后续预测的质量退化可能比 Transformer 的 KV cache 不一致更严重。
258	
259	---
260	
261	## 8. Hybrid Attention + Speculative Decoding Verify
262	
263	### 8.1 Nemotron 3 Super — MTP + Hybrid Mamba-Transformer（arXiv:2604.12374, 2026, NVIDIA）
264	
265	MTP head 与主模型共享参数，通过 shared-weight formulation 递归使用。Hybrid Mamba-2 + MoE + 少量 attention 层。MTP 平均 acceptance length = 3.45（SPEED-Bench, draft length=7）。
266	
267	**未讨论** Mamba 层的 state 管理（回滚/快照）问题——推测是因为 MTP verify 时 SSM 层的 state 按正确序列自然递推，不需要显式回滚。
268	
269	### 8.2 DUET — Disaggregated Hybrid Mamba-Transformer（arXiv:2603.15530, 2026）
270	
271	Hybrid Mamba-Transformer 模型的 SSM 层在 decode 阶段是 element-wise 操作，不适合 matmul-centric 加速器。SSM decode 是 bandwidth-bound 的，verify 时串行递推 SSM 层的瓶颈是内存带宽而非计算量。
272	
273	### 8.3 Jamba / Zamba
274	
275	Jamba（arXiv:2403.19887, AI21 Labs）：交替 Transformer + Mamba 层 + MoE，52B/12B active。Zamba（arXiv:2405.16712, Zyphra）：Mamba backbone + 单一共享 attention module。两者均未涉及 speculative decoding。
276	
277	---
278	
279	## 9. 当前代码中的 Verify 实现（本地调查补充）
280	
281	### 9.1 已有的放松接受基础设施
282	
283	`demo-sala/sglang/` 中使用 `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`（sgl_kernel CUDA kernel），支持 `threshold_single` 和 `threshold_acc` 两个放松参数（默认 1.0 = 标准 lossless）。
284	
285	### 9.2 Phased Verify 的 GLA State 管理
286	
287	从 `eagle_worker.py` 和 `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` 代码可见：
288	
289	1. Phase-1 verify：`p1_gla = intermediate_ssm[:, :bs, :3].clone()`，保存 3 个 GLA intermediate state
290	2. Phase-1 结束后：将 Phase-1 的 dt1 state 写回 `ssm_states_all`，然后执行 Phase-2
291	3. Phase-2 结束后：恢复 Phase-1 的 GLA intermediate state `intermediate_ssm[:, :bs, :3] = p1_gla`，同时保存 Phase-2 的 state
292	4. 恢复生产 ssm_states：`ssm_states_all[:, mamba_indices_active] = ssm_orig_backup`
293	
294	这本质上是多阶段 state snapshot + restore 策略，对应 SpecMamba 论文的 Plan I 变体。
295	
296	### 9.3 文献中的空白
297	
298	**目前没有发现任何论文专门解决"混合 standard attention + GLA 架构的 speculative decoding verify"问题**。现有工作要么：
299	- 全 SSM（SpecMamba）：target 全部是 Mamba
300	- 全 Transformer target（Mamba Drafters）：SSM 只做 drafter
301	- MTP self-speculation（Nemotron）：不涉及外部 drafter 的 verify 回滚
302	
303	MiniCPM-SALA 的 8 层 attention + 24 层 GLA + EAGLE 外部 drafter 组合在文献中独一无二。
304	
305	---

307	## 10. Draft 生成方式革新影响 Verify
308	
309	### 10.1 FastEagle — Cascaded Drafting（arXiv:2509.20416, 2025）
310	
311	非自回归级联 drafter，一次 forward 生成整个 draft。Constrained draft tree 保持无损验证成本。在 greedy 和 stochastic decoding 下一致超过 EAGLE-3。
312	
313	### 10.2 DDTree — Block Diffusion Draft Trees（arXiv:2604.12989, 2026）
314	
315	从 block diffusion drafter 的 per-position distributions 直接构建 draft tree。Best-first heap 选择最可能匹配 target 的 continuation。单次 target forward 验证整棵树。
316	
317	### 10.3 SpecForge（arXiv:2603.18567, 2026）
318	
319	SGLang 官方 EAGLE-3 训练框架。发布 SpecBundle：主流开源 LLM 的生产级 EAGLE-3 draft 模型。Qwen3-235B-A22B 训练加速 9.9x。
320	
321	### 10.4 PayPal EAGLE3 实证研究（arXiv:2604.19767, 2026）
322	
323	vLLM + EAGLE3 + 2xH100。gamma=3: 22-49% throughput 提升，18-33% 延迟降低。Acceptance rate ~35.5% (gamma=3), ~25% (gamma=5)。
324	
325	---
326	
327	## 11. Verify 后处理与 KV Cache 管理
328	
329	### 11.1 Sparse Verification（arXiv:2512.21911, 2025）
330	
331	对验证阶段做联合稀疏化（attention + FFN + MoE），减少验证计算瓶颈。Inter-draft token 和 inter-layer retrieval reuse 减少冗余计算。适用场景：长上下文和 MoE 模型。
332	
333	### 11.2 EAGLE-Pangu — 加速器安全树 SD（arXiv:2603.08088, 2026）
334	
335	将 EAGLE-3 树推测解码移植到 Ascend NPU。显式 branch/commit cache manager；加速器安全树张量化（消除负索引）；fused-kernel 兼容的 teacher 验证路径。
336	
337	### 11.3 Nightjar — 资源感知自适应（arXiv:2512.22420, 2025）
338	
339	根据请求负载动态选择最优 speculative length。MAB planner 决定何时禁用推测。高负载时验证开销变为瓶颈。
340	
341	### 11.4 SMART — System-Aware Marginal Analysis（arXiv:2604.09731, 2026）
342	
343	将树展开重形式化为硬件感知优化问题。边际收益-成本规则，仅当节点边际收益-成本比超过树级加速比时才展开。Training-free，即插即用。

404	
405	## 13. 第三轮补充调查（2026-04-27）
406	
407	### 13.1 SSM State Checkpoint/Rollback 新发现
408	
409	**Snakes and Ladders: Accelerating SSM Inference with Speculative Decoding**（arXiv:2402.00550, NeurIPS 2024 Workshop, UCLA + AWS AI）
410	
411	两种 SSM state backtracking 方法：
412	- **Activation Replay**：缓存 SSM block 的输入激活，回溯时只重跑 state update kernel 到最后验证通过的 token
413	- **Joint Attainment and Advancement**：在验证当前 draft 的同时前进一步，恢复到最后验证通过的 token 的 SSM state
414	
415	与 SpecMamba 的 Plan I/II 方案互补，但仅处理纯 SSM target。
416	
417	**STree**（arXiv:2505.14969, NeurIPS 2025）
418	
419	将 token tree 压平为单一序列 + tree mask，利用 SSM 状态转移矩阵的可加性，一次性前向计算 tree 上所有节点的输出，避免为每条路径重复展开 SSM。提出 custom tree scan kernel。明确声称适用于"hybrid SSM+Transformer"架构，但论文中的 hybrid 是指 Mamba+Attention 层交替排列的 target model，不处理外部 drafter。
420	
421	### 13.2 混合架构 + Spec Decoding 工程实践
422	
423	**SGLang MambaRadixCache + Speculative Decoding**（PyTorch Blog "Hybrid Models Meet SGLang"）
424	
425	已在 Qwen3-Next（Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention 混合）上验证的关键设计：
426	- **双内存池设计**：Mamba pool + KV cache pool 独立管理
427	- **MambaRadixCache**：混合 radix tree，分别管理 SSM state 和 KV cache 的 prefix 匹配
428	- **State Snapshotting**：为每个 draft token 分配独立的 Mamba cache slot，解决 SSM state 不可逆问题
429	- **EAGLE-Tree with top-K > 1**：支持树形 draft + 混合架构
430	
431	**这是 MiniCPM-SALA 最直接可借鉴的工程实现**。
432	
433	**Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs**（arXiv:2411.19379, MLSys 2025 Outstanding Paper Honorable Mention）
434	
435	第一个支持混合模型 prefix caching 的系统。SSM state 不可逆（只能精确匹配，不能部分重叠），采用审慎的 admission 策略——只在高复用概率时缓存 SSM state。SSM state 的 "all-or-nothing" 特性分析对理解 GLA verify 挑战很有价值。
436	
437	**Qwen3.5-27B 的 recurrent state 问题**（vLLM 论坛）
438	
439	Qwen3.5 的 conv_states 和 recurrent_states **没有 sequence_length 维度**，无法像 KV cache 那样选择性接受部分 token。如果 draft 包含 4 个 token 但 target 只接受前 2 个，系统无法恢复对应的 conv_states 和 recurrent_states。因此 Qwen3.5 目前只支持 MTP-1。
440	
441	**这正是 MiniCPM-SALA 的 GLA 层的核心挑战的直接映射**——recurrent state 是整体更新的，无法按 token 粒度截断。
442	
443	**vLLM GDN Attention Bug**（issue #38196）
444	
445	GDN（Gated DeltaNet）attention backend 在 ngram speculative decoding 产生 mixed decode + spec_decode batch 时崩溃。GDN builder 假设 num_decodes 和 num_spec_decodes 互斥，但部分拒绝时两者同时非零。
446	
447	**直接证明工业界在混合 linear attention 层的 speculative decoding 实现上存在基础性 bug**。
448	
449	### 13.3 Linear Attention + Speculative Decoding 兼容性
450	
451	**When Linear Attention Meets Autoregressive Decoding**（arXiv:2406.07368, ICML 2024, Georgia Tech + Google）
452	
453	第一个系统研究 linear attention 与 speculative decoding 的兼容性。发现：
454	- 标准 linear attention 的 causal mask 与 tree attention mask 不兼容
455	- 提出 local augmentation 技术增强 linear attention 的局部特征提取
456	- 开发 tree-based attention 与 linear attention 的无缝集成方案
457	
458	**高度相关**：论文直接解决了 linear attention 层在 tree verify 中的 causal mask 问题。
459	
460	### 13.4 Cactus 完整算法
461	
462	**Cactus**（arXiv:2604.04987, ICLR 2026 Poster）
463	
464	约束优化目标：最大化接受率，约束 KL(h || q) ≤ delta。
465	
466	最优解（Corollary 5，KL 散度 + 二阶 Taylor 近似）：
467	```
468	gamma* = min{q(n) + sqrt(2 * delta * q(n) * (1-q(n))), 1}
469	```
470	
471	q(n) 是 target model 对 draft token n 的概率。gamma* 给 draft token n 一个 "bonus probability"，bonus 最大值在 q(n)=0.5 时取得。
472	
473	delta 典型值：0.01~0.05。
474	
475	对 tree verify：理论上可以嵌入（每条边的 gamma* 不同），但论文未做 tree verify 实验。
476	
477	代码：https://github.com/MANGA-UOFA/Cactus
478	
479	### 13.5 MARS 完整算法
480	
481	**MARS**（arXiv:2601.15498, ICLR 2026）
482	
483	对每个 draft token v_t：
484	1. **Exact Match**：如果 v_t = target top-1，直接接受
485	2. **Adaptive Relaxation**：如果 v_t = target top-2 且 `r_t > theta`，接受（视为 tie）
486	3. **Rejection**：否则拒绝
487	
488	核心度量 **Logit Ratio**：`r_t = z_{(2)} / z_{(1)}`（top-2 logit / top-1 logit）
489	
490	theta **固定 0.9**，ablation 在 [0.85, 0.95] 稳定。
491	
492	实验数据：
493	
494	| Model | EAGLE-3 | MARS |
495	|-------|---------|------|
496	| Vicuna-13B | 3.12x / tau=5.64 | **3.74x / tau=7.20** |
497	| Llama-3.1-8B | 3.24x / tau=4.82 | **4.00x / tau=6.61** |
498	| Llama-3.1-70B | 4.61x / tau=5.86 | **4.76x / tau=6.53** |
499	
500	与 tree verify 兼容：每条边的验证独立应用 MARS 规则。
501	
502	代码：https://github.com/5SSjw/MARS
503	
504	### 13.6 SMC-SD 完整实现
505	
506	**SMC-SD**（arXiv:2604.15672）
507	
508	基于 SGLang fork，3 步循环：Extend → Reweight → Resample。
509	
510	ESS（Effective Sample Size）：`ESS = (sum w_n)^2 / sum w_n^2`。ESS 趋近 1 说明权重退化，需要 resample。
511	
512	粒子数 N：实验中 N=4~8。Roofline 模型分析：N 应选择使算术强度接近 GPU roofline ridge point。
513	
514	理论误差界（Theorem 3.1）：L2 bias = `O((1 + chi^2(p||q)) / N)`，L1 bias = `O(sqrt(...))`
515	
516	实验：比 optimized SD 快 2.36x，比 AR 快 5.2x，准确率在 target 3% 以内。
517	
518	代码：https://github.com/abdelfattah-lab/smcsd
519	
520	### 13.7 2026 最新论文
521	
522	**HSD: Hierarchical Speculative Decoding**（ICLR 2026 Oral）
523	
524	解决 sequence-level verification 的"联合不可解性"问题。将 resampling 组织为层次结构，在分支间重新分配概率质量。集成 EAGLE-3 获 **12% 性能提升**。Lossless。
525	
526	**SSD/Saguaro: Speculative Speculative Decoding**（ICLR 2026 Poster）
527	
528	将 draft 和 verify 阶段并行化。verify 进行时，draft model 预测 verify 结果并提前准备下一轮 speculation。比 SD baseline 快 **2x**，比 AR 快 5x。
529	
530	**LTD: Learning To Draft**（ICLR 2026 Poster）
531	
532	将 draft-verify 建模为 RL 环境，训练 co-adaptive policies 动态协调 draft 和 verify。直接优化 throughput，2.24x-4.32x 加速，**比 EAGLE-3 优 36.4%**。
533	
534	**DDTree + DFlash**（arXiv:2604.12989, 2026.04）
535	
536	从 block diffusion drafter 的 per-position 边缘分布构建 draft tree。Best-first heap 算法最大化期望接受长度。接受长度提升 **35%-63%**，峰值 8.22x 加速。已在 RTX 3090/DGX Spark 社区验证。
537	
538	**FLy: Accepting Semantically Correct Drafts Beyond Exact Match**（AMD ROCm Blog）
539	
540	Entropy-based gating + deferred window validation，允许语义正确但词汇不同的 draft 被接受。99%+ accuracy recovery。
541	
542	**RACER**（arXiv:2604.14885）
543	
544	AC 自动机 + LRU 淘汰构建 n-gram retrieval tree，与 logits tree 融合。Training-free，plug-and-play。
545	
546	**Super Apriel**（arXiv:2604.19877）
547	
548	15B supernet，每层 4 种 mixer（FA/SWA/KDA/GDN），运行时可切换。共享 checkpoint 可直接做 self-speculative decoding，无需单独 draft model。DIL/KIL 初始化方法可将 GDN/KDA 层注入已有 transformer。
549	
550	**Mamba-3**（arXiv:2603.15569, ICLR 2026 Oral）
551	
552	Trapezoidal discretization + MIMO + 复值状态更新。1.5B scale 用一半状态大小匹配 Mamba-2 perplexity。
553	
554	**ConFu: Contemplate the Future**（arXiv:2603.08899）
555	
556	通过 contemplate tokens 和 soft prompts 让 draft model 获取 target model 的"未来信号"。
557	
558	### 13.8 SGLang 工程实现细节
559	
560	**SGLang Adaptive Speculative Decoding**（已落地）：
561	- EMA 策略：每轮 verify 后读取 accepted draft length，用指数移动平均平滑
562	- 预建候选层：启动时为每个候选 tier（默认 [1,3,7]）预建 CudaGraphRunner
563	- **当前限制**：只支持 `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` + `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`
564	
565	**Tree Verify Kernel**：
566	- Greedy 路径：`verify_tree_greedy_func()` 调用 `sgl_kernel.verify_tree_greedy` CUDA kernel
567	- Sampling 路径：`tree_speculative_sampling_target_only()` kernel
568	- **draft_probs = torch.zeros(...)**：当前代码走 target-only 验证，不使用 draft model 的概率分布
569	
570	**SGLang 最新 spec 算法扩展**：
571	- **P-EAGLE**（Issue #23171）：并行 EAGLE，一次 forward 生成所有 K 个 draft token
572	- **DDTree**（Issue #22887）：扩散 draft tree
573	- **SSD/Saguaro**（Issue #19896）：异步推测解码
574	- **Spec V2**（`SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2`）：STANDALONE draft model
575	
576	### 13.9 量化 + Spec Decoding 实践
577	
578	**QSpec**（arXiv:2410.11305, EMNLP 2025 / ICLR 2025 提交）：
579	- W4A4 做 draft（快但不准），W4A16 做 verify（准但慢），**共享权重和 KV cache**
580	- 接受率 93-95%，加速 1.64-1.80x，无质量损失
581	- **不适用 NVFP4**：需要 W4A4 kernel，sm_120 无此 kernel
582	
583	**SpecMQuant**（arXiv:2505.22179）：
584	- **4-bit 量化模型上 tree-style verify 时间开销远大于 single-token forward pass**
585	- 解决方案：层次化框架，用小模型做中间阶段将 tree drafts 转为 sequence drafts
586	- W4A16 Llama-3-70B 上 **2.78x** 加速，比 EAGLE-2 快 1.31x
587	
588	**NVFP4 target logits 精度**：
589	- NVIDIA 数据：DeepSeek-R1-0528 从 FP8 到 NVFP4 精度差 <1%（MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond）
590	- vLLM：MTP spec + Marlin NVFP4 路径 -22% throughput（activation distribution mismatch）
591	- 关键问题：放松验证叠加量化误差，MARS 的 logit ratio 在量化 logits 上可能更不稳定
592	
593	### 13.10 生产环境 Spec Decoding 经验
594	
595	**Acceptance Rate 与加速比**：
596	- alpha=0.6 → ~2.4x 加速
597	- alpha=0.8 → ~3.7x 加速
598	- **alpha < 0.5 时 spec decode 比 baseline 更慢**
599	
600	**Batch Size 与 Spec Decoding**：
601	- bs 1-4：GPU memory-bound，spec 有效
602	- bs 8-32：过渡区域
603	- bs 32+：compute-bound，spec 通常更慢
604	- **长上下文反转**：MagicDec 发现当 KV cache 成为瓶颈时，大 batch + 长上下文 spec 仍可 2x 加速
605	
606	**Acceptance Rate 波动**：
607	- 代码生成 alpha ~70-80%，数学推理 50-60%，开放聊天 40-60%
608	- 同一请求内位置方差极大；请求间方差大 → ragged tensor
609	- 生产部署通常比实验室数据低 40-60%
610	
611	### 13.11 文献空白确认（第三轮）
612	
613	经三轮系统性搜索，**确认不存在**专门解决"混合 standard attention + GLA/SSM target model + 外部 EAGLE drafter 的 tree verify + GLA state checkpoint/rollback"的论文。
614	
615	最接近的四个方案：
616	1. **SGLang MambaRadixCache + per-draft-token Mamba cache slot**（工程方案，Qwen3-Next 上已验证）
617	2. **STree 的累积状态转移矩阵**（理论方案，custom GLA tree scan kernel）
618	3. **Snakes & Ladders 的 Activation Replay**（baseline 方案，缓存输入激活重算）
619	4. **Qwen3.5/vLLM 的现状**（反面教训：recurrent state 无 sequence_length 维度）
620	
621	### 13.12 方法组合兼容性
622	
623	- **MARS + Traversal Verification**：可叠加（MARS 改单 token 判定，Traversal 改 tree 遍历策略）
624	- **MARS + Block Verification**：可叠加但需重新推导 BV 最优性
625	- **Cactus + Block Verification**：可叠加（Cactus 修改的分布 h 嵌入 BV 框架）
626	- **SMC-SD + 其他方法**：基本不兼容（不同范式：resampling vs rejection）
627	- **推荐组合**：MARS（最易）→ Traversal Verification（可叠加）→ Block Verification（lossless +5-8%）
628

## Top 10 文献 ROI 排序

ROI 评估维度：对 MiniCPM-SALA 当前架构（单卡 RTX 6000D、NVFP4、EAGLE-3 chain verify、24 GLA + 8 sparse attention、不可换模型/换 draft）的**落地成本 × 预期收益**。

---

### 1. MARS — Margin-Aware Speculative Verification
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2601.15498, ICLR 2026 |
| **预期收益** | accept length +17-28%（Vicuna-13B tau 5.64→7.20），直接提升 E2E 吞吐 |
| **落地成本** | **极低**——纯算法改动，改 `eagle_info.py` 的 verify 规则即可；`r_t = z_(2)/z_(1) > theta(=0.9)` 一行判断；training-free |
| **风险** | 量化 logit 精度可能影响 logit ratio 稳定性（需实测 theta 在 NVFP4 上是否仍稳定） |
| **与现有代码关系** | 代码已有 `threshold_single/threshold_acc` 参数，MARS 可直接映射为修改 threshold 逻辑 |
| **ROI 理由** | 改动量最小（~50 行 Python），收益有论文数据支撑，无需训练/新硬件/新 kernel |

### 2. HSD — Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2601.05724, ICLR 2026 Oral |
| **预期收益** | 集成 EAGLE-3 **+12%**；对 chain verify 和 tree verify 均有效 |
| **落地成本** | **低**——替换 `verify_tree_greedy` 的扫描逻辑，从 top-down 改为 bottom-up + hierarchical branch resampling；training-free；纯 Python 算法层 |
| **风险** | Capped Branch Resampling 需要推导 GLA state 的对应 rollback（当前 verify 后已有 `_mamba_verify_update`，需适配新 accept 位置） |
| **ROI 理由** | ICLR Oral 理论保障 + 实测 +12%；与 MARS 正交可叠加；代码已开源 |

### 3. VOCABTRIM — Draft 词表裁剪
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2506.22694 |
| **预期收益** | vocab 73448→32000（当前已有 draft_vocab_size=32000 但 **target forward 仍计算 73448 logits**）；裁剪 target verify 的 LM head 计算可省 ~56% |
| **落地成本** | **极低**——在 target verify forward 后截断 logits 到 draft 词表范围，或用 `d2t` 映射只算 32K logit；training-free |
| **风险** | bonus token 采样需从完整 73448 词表采（约 0.2% 概率需要完整词表），需 fallback 路径 |
| **ROI 理由** | 当前 verify 阶段的 logit 计算（73448 dim）是显存/计算热点，裁剪直接砍一半；改动极小 |

### 4. GOOSE — Anisotropic Spine Tree
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2604.02047, 2026.04 |
| **预期收益** | 比 balanced-tree **+12-33%**；当前 dtn=5 tree-aware verify 已落地，GOOSE 是同方向改进 |
| **落地成本** | **低**——改 `eagle_info.py` 的树构建逻辑：high-confidence token 拉深链 + 每节点挂宽分支；training-free |
| **风险** | 需要 n-gram retrieval（context-matched token），需在 SGLang 的 draft 路径中嵌入 n-gram 索引 |
| **ROI 理由** | 与已落地的 tree-aware dtn5 verify 天然兼容；无需训练；直接改树形状即可 |

### 5. FASER — Fine-Grained Phase Management
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2604.20503, 2026.04 |
| **预期收益** | throughput **+53%**，latency **-1.92x**；与 Phased Verify（已实现但未启用）方向完全一致 |
| **落地成本** | **中低**——需改造现有 Phased Verify 代码，增加 per-request 动态 speculative length + verification chunk 拆分；training-free |
| **风险** | Phased Verify 当前有 GLA state 近似问题（Phase-2 用 Phase-1 最终 state，累积误差未量化） |
| **ROI 理由** | 代码中 Phased Verify 框架已存在（`EAGLE_PHASED_VERIFY=1`），FASER 是该方向的自然进化 |

### 6. Nightjar — 自适应 Spec 开关
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2512.22420, 2025.12 |
| **预期收益** | throughput **+27%**，latency **-20%**；避免 accept rate 低时 spec 反而拖慢 |
| **落地成本** | **低**——MAB（多臂老虎机）决策器，根据历史 accept rate 动态开关 spec；training-free |
| **风险** | 需要在 SGLang 的调度循环中嵌入 MAB 逻辑；accept_rate 坍缩场景下自动降级是刚需 |

### 7. SAGE — Entropy-Guided Adaptive Tree
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2602.00523, 2026.02 |
| **预期收益** | 3.36x speedup；高置信时深窄树（提升 accept），低置信时浅宽树（减少浪费） |
| **落地成本** | **低**——entropy 可从 draft model 的 softmax 输出直接获取，无需额外计算；改树构建策略即可；training-free |
| **风险** | 需要为多种树形状预建 CUDA graph（当前 SGLang adaptive spec 已有 [1,3,7] 三级候选） |
| **ROI 理由** | 与 SGLang adaptive speculative decoding 的 EMA 策略互补；entropy 比 EMA 更具前瞻性 |

### 8. Traversal Verification
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2505.12398, NeurIPS 2025 |
| **预期收益** | 接受概率 +2-17%（温度越高收益越大）；序列级联合概率补偿 |
| **落地成本** | **中低**——需改 verify 的遍历方向（top-down → bottom-up）和采样逻辑；与 FlashInfer kernel 兼容 |
| **风险** | 当前 `verify_tree_greedy` 是 CUDA kernel，需修改或替换为 bottom-up 遍历；GLA state rollback 需适配新遍历顺序 |
| **ROI 理由** | 纯算法改动无损；与 MARS/HSD 正交可叠加；但需要 kernel 层改动，成本高于 MARS |

### 9. Quasar — 量化验证
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2603.01399, 2026.03 |
| **预期收益** | 验证阶段减半内存流量；对 NVFP4 target 的 verify 计算瓶颈直接有效 |
| **落地成本** | **中**——verify 阶段用更低精度 forward（FP8 或 INT8）；需要确保 logit 精度足够做 accept/reject 判断 |
| **风险** | NVFP4 已经是 4-bit 权重，进一步量化激活可能影响 logit 分布精度，特别是 MARS 的 logit ratio 敏感度 |
| **ROI 理由** | 当前 verify 的 GEMM 是 decode 期瓶颈之一；但需要量化精度验证 |

### 10. SMART — System-Aware Marginal Analysis
| | |
|---|---|
| **arXiv** | 2604.09731, 2026 |
| **预期收益** | 树展开的硬件感知优化，避免过度展开导致的 verify 开销浪费 |
| **落地成本** | **低**——边际收益-成本比规则，可嵌入 `eagle_info.py` 的树构建；training-free |

| **ROI 理由** | 对 dtn=5 的树展开做硬件感知截断，避免 verify 阶段处理低质量分支 |

Title: Cactus: Accelerating Auto-Regressive Decoding with Constrained Acceptance Speculative Sampling [Quick Review]
URL: https://liner.com/review/cactus-accelerating-autoregressive-decoding-with-constrained-acceptance-speculative-sampling
Content: ## Proposed method

## Proposed method

 We introduce Cactus (constrained acceptance speculative sampling), a principled modification enforcing a hard constraint on distributional divergence while enabling higher acceptance rates.

 Cactus reformulates speculative sampling as a constrained optimization problem, explicitly balancing acceptance rate and divergence from the verifier's distribution.

 The method uses only KL divergence as the distance measure, with an approximated solution increasing the candidate token's probability based on the verifier's confidence and a divergence parameter. [...] Speculative sampling (SpS) has been successful in accelerating the decoding throughput of auto-regressive large language models by leveraging smaller draft models. SpS strictly enforces the generated distribution to match that of the verifier LLM. This is unnecessarily restrictive as slight variations of the verifier's distribution, such as sampling with top-$k$ or temperature, would also be acceptable. Typical acceptance sampling (TAS) alleviates this issue by accepting more tokens using entropy-based heuristics. However, this approach distorts the verifier distribution, potentially degrading output quality when the verifier encodes critical information. In this work, we formalize the speculative sampling algorithm through the lens of constrained optimization. Based on this formulation, [...] of constrained optimization. Based on this formulation, we propose Cactus (\\c\\onstrained \\ac\\cep\\t\\ance spec\\u\\lative \\s\\ampling), a method that guarantees controlled divergence from the verifier distribution and increasing acceptance rates. Empirical results across a wide range of benchmarks confirm the effectiveness of our approach.

[...] foundation in constrained optimization and demonstrating practical robustness across diverse tasks. [...] Here, we produce data points by running grid search on \delta for Cactus and interpolation rate \alpha for interpolation, respectively. As shown, Cactus consistently outperforms interpolation at the similar acceptance rate. For example, at a similar acceptance rate of approximately 90%, Cactus achieves a score above 86 (\delta=1e4) on GSM8K, whereas interpolation only reaches a score below 72 (\alpha=0.9). Notably, even at a 96.3% acceptance rate, Cactus maintains a higher score (above 80), further confirming the necessity of divergence control in our method.

# Cactus: Accelerating Auto-Regressive Decoding with Constrained Acceptance Speculative Sampling

UAlberta

## Abstract

Speculative sampling methods are enhanced by formulating them as constrained optimization problems, enabling controlled distribution divergence while maintaining high acceptance rates and output quality.

[...] Exponential Cone Programming: For distributionally robust optimization (DRO), KL divergence is epigraph-representable by exponential cones (e.g., MOSEK supports triplet constraints (p^​s​,ps​,−δs​)∈Kexp​), leading to a tractable conic program for robustifying empirical distributions. This admits strong duality and is highly scalable for classical DRO settings (Kocuk, 2020).
 Sequential Convex Programming: In nonconvex/constrained problems (including those with a local Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz (KL) property), SCP (Yu et al., 2020, Lu et al., 1 Oct 2025) iteratively solves convex majorant subproblems with penalty or linesearch, ensuring convergence (often globally) under mild assumptions. Content: When given the reward function r(y|x), the base model is fine-tuned using reinforcement learning to maximize the reward under certain constraints. From an optimization perspective, this step is equivalent to solving the following constrained optimization problem: max π Eπ[r(y|x)] −βDf(π, πref) s.t.
X y π(y|x) = 1 and π(y|x) ≥0 ∀y.
The two constraints are introduced to ensure that the solution is a valid distribution, though in prac-tice we don’t need to explicitly deal with them. To solve the constrained problem, we can apply the Lagrange multiplier, which gives us L(π, λ, α) = Eπ[r(y|x)] −βEπref  f  π(y|x) πref(y|x)  −λ X y π(y|x) −1 ! [...] Fortunately, we will show that, by carefully analyzing the normalization constant Z(x), we can derive a closed-form solution for many other (but not all) divergences as well, without the need to estimate the normalization constant Z(x). To achieve this, we can first rewrite π⋆(y|x) in the following format using the dual variables λ and α(y): π⋆(y|x) = πref(y|x)(f ′)−1 r(y|x) −λ + α(y) β  .

The original DPO method (Rafailov et al., 2023) estab-lishes a functional mapping between the reward model and the optimal policy under the reverse KL divergence constraint. This allows for the direct optimization of the policy by reparameterizing the reward function using the policy (i.e., the language model) in a supervised manner, r(·|x) = β log πθ(·|x) πref(·|x) + β log Z(x).

Speculative sampling (SpS) has been successful in accelerating the decoding throughput of auto-regressive large language models by leveraging smaller draft models. SpS strictly enforces the generated distribution to match that of the verifier LLM. This is unnecessarily restrictive as slight variations of the verifier’s distribution, such as sampling with top-k or temperature, would also be acceptable. Typical acceptance sampling (TAS) alleviates this issue by accepting more tokens using entropy-based heuristics. However, this approach distorts the verifier distribution, potentially degrading output quality when the verifier encodes critical information. In this work,

Here, the KL divergence encourages h to focus on the mode of q (since h is the first argument), while the entropy term encourages h to be deterministic. However, the summation allows h to collapse into a deterministic distribution at the expense of increasing divergence, therefore failing to capture the full shape of q. In fact, TAS always yields h with entropy 0 while increasing the divergence by at least H(q). As a result, the produced distribution may diverge significantly from the verifier model, especially when q carries high entropy and thus rich information.

In addition to task scores, we report the average acceptance length (AL) for all runs. Specifically, AL m refers to the expected number of accepted tokens among m drafted tokens. A higher AL m generally indicates faster generation. However, a method may artificially inflate AL by accepting low-quality draft tokens that lead to longer, less efficient chains of thought. Although AL remains high in this case, the behavior can lead to lower overall throughput due to unnecessarily lengthy outputs. To present a more complete picture of generation efficiency, we also measure the number of rejected tokens during generation, which reflects both the acceptance rate and the total length of generation.

## Cactus — 约束接受推测采样

**论文**：arXiv:2604.04987，ICLR 2026 Poster，Yongchang Hao & Lili Mou，UAlberta

### 1. 它解决什么问题

标准 Speculative Sampling (SpS) 是**无损的**——输出分布严格等于 target 分布。但这"过于严格"了：top-k 采样、temperature 调整本来就会偏离 target 分布，只要偏离可控就完全可接受。

另一边，Typical Acceptance Sampling (TAS，Medusa 用的) 用 entropy 启发式放宽接受，accept rate 更高，但**分布变形不可控**——TAS 总是退化为确定性分布（entropy=0），KL 散度至少增加 H(q)，当 target 本身高熵时偏差巨大。

Cactus 的核心立场：**用约束优化取代启发式放松，保证输出分布与 target 的 KL 散度 ≤ δ**。

### 2. 理论框架：从 SpS 到约束优化

#### Observation 1（SpS 的统一视角）

任何目标分布 h 都可以被 draft-verify 框架精确产生，只要：

```
接受概率：  φ(x_t | x_{<t}) = min{h(x_t | x_{<t}) / p(x_t | x_{<t}), 1}
恢复分布：  g(x_t | x_{<t}) ∝ h(x_t | x_{<t}) - p(x_t | x_{<t}) · φ(x_t | x_{<t})
```

标准 SpS 就是取 `h = q`（target 分布）的特例。**换 h 就换接受规则**。

#### 约束优化问题

Cactus 把选 h 变成一个优化问题：

```
max   min{h_n / p(n), 1}        ← 最大化 draft token n 的接受概率
s.t.  h ∈ Δ^{|V|-1}            ← h 是合法概率分布
      D_f(h || q) ≤ δ           ← 与 target 的 f-散度不超过 δ
```

δ=0 时退化为标准 SpS（h=q），δ>0 时允许 h 偏离 q 以换取更高接受率。

### 3. 核心定理：最优解的结构

#### Theorem 2（一般 f-divergence）

最优 h 的结构出人意料地简洁：

```
h(i | x_{<t}) = γ*           如果 i = n（draft 采到的 token）
h(i | x_{<t}) = (1-γ*)/(1-q(n)) · q(i)   否则
```

其中 γ* 是以下方程在 [q(n), +∞) 上的根：

```
δ = q(n) · f(γ/q(n)) + (1-q(n)) · f((1-γ)/(1-q(n)))
```

**直觉**：最优策略就是给 draft token n 分配比 q(n) 更多的概率质量（"bonus"），其余 token 按比例缩放 q。所有额外概率都集中在 n 上。

#### Corollary 5（KL 散度的闭式解）

当 f-divergence 取 KL 散度时，方程没有闭式解。但 δ 通常很小，γ* 接近 q(n)，所以对 Φ(γ) = D_KL(h || q) 在 γ₀ = q(n) 处做二阶 Taylor 展开，得到：

```
γ* = min{q(n) + √(2δ · q(n) · (1-q(n))), 1}
```

**这是 Cactus 最核心的公式**。解读：

- 当 δ=0：γ* = q(n)，退化为标准 SpS
- δ 越大：γ* 越大，draft token 的"bonus"越多，接受率越高
- bonus 最大值在 q(n)=0.5 时取得（√(q·(1-q)) 最大），即 target 对 draft token 半信半疑时放松最有价值
- q(n) 接近 0 或 1 时 bonus 趋近 0——target 非常确定时没必要放松

### 4. Cactus 的接受规则

由 Observation 1，Cactus 的实际操作为：

```
接受概率：  φ(n | x_{<t}) = min{γ* / p(n), 1}
恢复分布：  g(i | x_{<t}) ∝ h(i) - p(i) · φ(i)
          = { (γ* - p(n)·φ(n)) / (1-Σ p(i)φ(i))   如果 i=n
            { (1-γ*)/(1-q(n)) · q(i) - p(i)·φ(i)) / (...)  否则
```

### 5. 与 TAS 和 Interpolation 的区别

| 方法 | 分布控制 | 接受率 | 质量保证 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SpS** | 严格无损 | 最低 | 完美 |
| **TAS** | 无保证（entropy=0 退化） | 高 | 不可控 |
| **Interpolation** `h=αq+(1-α)p` | 线性混合 | 中 | 无散度保证 |
| **Cactus** | KL(h\|\|q) ≤ δ | 高 | **有理论保证** |

论文的 Figure 2 直接对比 Cactus 和 Interpolation：相同接受率下 Cactus 的 task score 更高。例如 90% 接受率时 Cactus 在 GSM8K 上 >86 分，Interpolation <72 分。

### 6. 实验结果

Qwen3 系列，top-p=0.95, top-k=20, temperature=0.6：

**8B verifier + 0.6B drafter**（m=10）：

| 方法 | GSM8K Score | AL₁₀ | Rej↓ |
|---|---|---|---|
| SpS | 83.78 | 4.49 | Ref |
| TAS | 86.58 | 5.49 | -29% |
| Cactus δ=0.75 | 85.97 | 5.65 | -34% |
| Cactus δ=1.0 | 86.35 | 5.72 | -37% |

**14B verifier + 0.6B drafter**（m=10）：

| 方法 | GSM8K Score | AL₁₀ | Rej↓ |
|---|---|---|---|
| SpS | 91.89 | 5.11 | Ref |
| TAS | 92.87 | 6.78 | -32% |
| Cactus δ=0.75 | 92.15 | 7.15 | -36% |
| Cactus δ=1.0 | 92.87 | 7.00 | -34% |

**关键发现**：
- Cactus δ=1.0 在 0.6B+14B 上达到 **1.9× 加速**
- 拒绝 token 数减少 37-51%
- GPQA（高难度科学推理）上 Cactus 保持或超过 SpS 的准确率，TAS 反而下降
- δ 越大接受率越高但 task score 不是单调的：δ=0.75 在 GSM8K 上甚至比 δ=1.0 准确率更高

### 7. δ 的选择

δ 是 Cactus 唯一的超参数。论文实验中的取值：

- δ = 0.75：温和放松，质量几乎无损
- δ = 1.0：中等放松，最大接受率

δ 的含义是 `D_KL(h || q) ≤ δ`。在 nats 单位下：
- δ=1.0 意味着输出分布与 target 的 KL 散度不超过 1 nat
- 对比：TAS 的隐式 KL 散度通常 > H(q)，对于高熵分布可能 >> 1

论文没有给出通用的 δ 选择指南，但实验中 δ∈[0.75, 1.0] 对大多数任务效果稳定。

### 8. 与 Tree Verify 的兼容性

Cactus 理论上可以嵌入 tree verify：**每条边的验证独立应用 Cactus 规则**（不同边的 q(n) 不同，γ* 也不同）。但论文没有做 tree verify 实验，所有实验都是 chain verify。

### 9. 对 MiniCPM-SALA 的映射

当前代码中 `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` 已有 `threshold_single` 和 `threshold_acc` 参数（默认 1.0 = 标准 SpS）。Cactus 本质上就是把 threshold 从固定值 1.0 改为 `γ* / p(n)`，其中 γ* 由 δ 和 q(n) 决定。

但有一个关键差异：当前代码走 **target-only 验证**（`draft_probs = torch.zeros(...)`），即不使用 draft model 的概率分布。Cactus 需要 p(n) 来计算 γ*/p(n)。如果 p(n) 未知（target-only 模式），Cactus 不能直接使用——要么计算 draft probs，要么退化为 MARS 式的 logit ratio 方案。

代码：https://github.com/MANGA-UOFA/Cactus
